main_stories.title: Vance meets Italian PM Meloni during Milan Olympics visit
main_stories.narrative: MILAN, Italy — Vice President JD Vance met Friday with Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni during his weeklong visit to Italy for the Winter Olympics, according to the vice president's office. The hour-long meeting at the Prefettura di Milano was followed by a closed-door lunch, with only brief remarks open to the press. Vance's office said the leaders discussed bilateral relations, the Olympics and efforts to improve business and investment climate between the nations. Vance also attended the Olympics opening ceremony at San Siro Stadium with Secretary of State Marco Rubio.

main_stories.title: Starmer's chief of staff quits over Mandelson appointment
main_stories.narrative: LONDON, Britain — Prime Minister Keir Starmer's chief of staff Morgan McSweeney resigned Sunday, saying he took "full responsibility" for advising Starmer to appoint Peter Mandelson as U.S. ambassador despite Mandelson's known ties to Jeffrey Epstein. The departure comes amid mounting pressure on Starmer over the scandal, with some Labour lawmakers openly questioning his judgment and calling for his resignation. Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch said Starmer "has to take responsibility for his own terrible decisions," while Reform UK leader Nigel Farage said he believed Starmer's time would "soon be up." Starmer appointed deputy chiefs of staff Jill Cuthbertson and Vidhya Alakeson as acting replacements.

main_stories.title: Vatican Orders Removal of Meloni Face from Church Fresco
main_stories.narrative: ROME, Italy — The Vatican ordered the removal of Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni's face from a church fresco after it sparked controversy, according to the restorer who painted it. Bruno Valentinetti, 83, said he covered the face in the San Lorenzo in Lucina basilica "because the Vatican asked me to." The fresco had drawn crowds and criticism after Valentinetti painted what appeared to be Meloni's likeness on an angel figure during restoration work. Rome's vicariate said sacred art "cannot be subject to improper use or exploitation."

main_stories.title: Meloni calls Olympics protesters 'enemies of Italy'
main_stories.narrative: ROME, Italy — Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni called protesters who demonstrated against the Milan-Cortina 2026 Olympics "enemies of Italy and Italians" following clashes with police in Milan. "Thousands and thousands of Italians are working so that everything functions during the Olympics," Meloni said in a social media post Sunday. The prime minister condemned what she called "gangs of delinquents" after about 5,000 protesters marched through Milan, with some throwing stones at police near the Olympic Village area. Defense Minister Guido Crosetto and other government officials also condemned the violence, expressing solidarity with law enforcement.

main_stories.title: Uruguay's Orsi meets Xi, signs cooperation deals in Beijing
main_stories.narrative: BEIJING, China — Uruguayan President Yamandú Orsi met with Chinese President Xi Jinping on Tuesday, signing 12 cooperation documents covering areas from trade to the environment, according to China's official Xinhua news agency. Xi said China and Uruguay should work together to advance an "equal and orderly multipolar world," while Orsi called the strategic partnership between the nations at its "best moment." Both leaders committed to starting negotiations on a free trade deal between China and the South American trade bloc Mercosur, according to a joint statement. Orsi is leading a 150-member delegation including business leaders on a visit through February 7.

international_stories.title: Mexico to send humanitarian aid to Cuba by Monday
international_stories.narrative: MORELIA, Mexico — President Claudia Sheinbaum said Mexico will send humanitarian aid to Cuba by Monday, including food and basic supplies requested by the island nation. Sheinbaum said her government continues diplomatic talks with the United States to resume oil shipments to Cuba after President Donald Trump announced tariffs on countries supplying petroleum to the island. Foreign Minister Juan Ramón de la Fuente said Mexico will maintain humanitarian aid wherever required, stating the country's foreign policy follows constitutional principles and international law.

international_stories.title: Finland's Stubb says US ideology conflicts with Finnish values
international_stories.narrative: HELSINKI, Finland — Finnish President Alexander Stubb said Wednesday that the current U.S. administration's foreign policy is guided by an ideology that conflicts with Finnish values, citing America's undermining of international institutions and diminished focus on Europe. Speaking at the opening of Parliament, Stubb said Finland must acknowledge that the United States is changing in its approach to allies and foreign policy, though he called the U.S. an important ally. Stubb said the administration's 'Make America Great Again' ideology downplays the international rules-based order and the European Union, areas where Finland disagrees with Washington. Finland will update its foreign and security policy doctrine to reflect changes in the international situation, Stubb told lawmakers.

international_stories.title: Zelenskyy says Russia broke energy strike pause promise
international_stories.narrative: KYIV, Ukraine — President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Tuesday that Russia violated its promise to pause strikes on Ukrainian energy infrastructure after four days, breaking an arrangement requested by the United States. Zelenskyy said the pause began overnight into Friday but Russia resumed attacks despite temperatures below minus 20 degrees Celsius across much of Ukraine. President Donald Trump had stated January 29 that he personally asked Russian leader Vladimir Putin to halt strikes on Ukraine for one week due to severe cold, and Putin reportedly agreed. Zelenskyy said Ukraine was ready to reciprocate if Russia complied with the U.S. proposal.

international_stories.title: Russia breaks energy strike pause, Ukraine president says
international_stories.narrative: KYIV, Ukraine — Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Tuesday that Russia violated a promised pause in strikes on energy infrastructure after four days, breaking an arrangement reportedly brokered by U.S. President Donald Trump. Zelenskyy said the pause began Friday but Russia resumed attacks despite temperatures below minus 20 degrees Celsius across much of Ukraine. Trump had stated Monday that Russian leader Vladimir Putin agreed to halt energy strikes for one week due to severe cold conditions. Zelenskyy said Ukraine would contact American officials about the violation and expected continued partner support for the country's defense.

international_stories.title: Tusk defends parliament speaker after US cuts diplomatic contact
international_stories.narrative: WARSAW, Poland — Prime Minister Donald Tusk defended Poland's parliament speaker Thursday after the U.S. ambassador severed diplomatic contact over criticism of President Donald Trump. Ambassador Tom Rose said he would end all communication with Parliament Speaker Wlodzimierz Czarzasty after Czarzasty refused to support Trump's Nobel Peace Prize nomination, calling Trump's policies destabilizing. "Allies should respect, not lecture, each other. At least this is how we here in Poland understand partnership," Tusk wrote on social media platform X. Rose responded that Czarzasty's "outrageous and unprovoked insults" against Trump had become "a serious impediment" to U.S.-Polish relations.

international_stories.title: Poland Ready to Transfer MiG-29 Jets to Ukraine
international_stories.narrative: KYIV, Ukraine — Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said Poland is prepared to transfer MiG-29 fighter jets to Ukraine if needed, following discussions with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy during a visit to Kyiv on Tuesday. Tusk said the MiG jets are available and ready for transfer, though he declined to specify whether other aircraft types could be considered as alternatives. The leaders also signed a letter of intent for joint production of ammunition and military equipment, with Tusk stating that Poland and Ukraine will build factories together using European, Polish and Ukrainian funding. Tusk emphasized that Ukraine has become "perhaps the most valuable partner for any country that wants to modernize its armaments."

domestic_stories.title: Canada drops EV sales quota amid auto industry pressure
domestic_stories.narrative: VAUGHAN, Ontario — Prime Minister Mark Carney announced Thursday that Canada will scrap its electric vehicle sales mandate, replacing the controversial policy with stricter tailpipe emissions standards and new purchase incentives. The government will eliminate the Electric Vehicle Availability Standard that required 100% zero-emission vehicle sales by 2035, responding to pressure from auto manufacturers and provincial leaders who called the timeline unrealistic. Carney said the new approach "focuses on the results that matter to Canadians, while avoiding placing undue burdens on the Canadian auto industry." The revised strategy aims for 75% EV adoption by 2035 and includes $2.3 billion in purchase incentives for vehicles under $50,000.

main_stories.title: France accuses Russia of Epstein smear campaign against Macron
main_stories.narrative: PARIS, France — French authorities said they detected a Russian disinformation operation that falsely linked President Emmanuel Macron to the Jeffrey Epstein scandal, a government source told Agence France-Presse on Friday. The campaign involved creating a fake website impersonating the news outlet France-Soir and publishing fabricated articles connecting Macron to the convicted sex offender, the source said. France's Viginum agency, which monitors foreign interference operations, attributed the effort to the Russian Storm-1516 network with "high degree of confidence," according to the source. The disinformation was then amplified on social media platform X through accounts monitored by French authorities.

international_stories.title: France adopts 2026 budget boosting military spending
international_stories.narrative: PARIS, France — France adopted its delayed 2026 budget Monday, clearing the way for higher military spending promised by President Emmanuel Macron to confront threats linked to Russia's war in Ukraine and Middle East conflicts. Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu used special constitutional power to pass the bill without a parliamentary vote after lawmakers proved unable to reach a compromise. The Defense Ministry will receive an additional 6.7 billion euros ($7.9 billion) compared to 2025, funding a new nuclear-powered attack submarine, 362 armored vehicles and new surface-to-air missiles. The government is targeting a budget deficit of 5% of gross domestic product, down from 5.4% in 2025.

domestic_stories.title: France to send fertility letters to all 29-year-olds
domestic_stories.narrative: PARIS, France — The French government will send letters to all 29-year-old citizens this summer as part of a new fertility plan aimed at boosting the country's declining birth rate, Health Minister Stéphanie Rist said Thursday. The initiative includes 16 measures to combat infertility, including creating a national portal on reproductive health and strengthening sex education in schools, Rist stated. France recorded more deaths than births for the first time since World War II in 2025, with only 645,000 babies born compared to 651,000 deaths, according to INSEE statistics. The plan supports President Emmanuel Macron's promised "demographic rearmament" announced in 2024, officials said.

domestic_stories.title: Macron meets farmers ahead of agriculture fair visit
domestic_stories.narrative: PARIS, France — President Emmanuel Macron met with agricultural organizations at the Elysee Palace on Monday and visited a farm in Haute-Saone on Tuesday, seeking to reassure farmers ahead of the upcoming Agriculture Fair. The meetings come as agricultural anger persists over issues including the Mercosur trade deal and international competition, despite France's rejection of the trade agreement. The FNSEA union described Monday's exchange as "correct" but lacking ambition, while the Peasant Confederation called it "disappointing." Macron said France faces "an enormous agricultural challenge" and promised "very concrete responses" in coming weeks.

The allegations emerged as France's parliament adopted a 2026 budget that increases military spending, with officials citing Russian threats as justification for the defense increases. main_stories.title: Sheinbaum declares Mexico will not bow to foreign interference
main_stories.narrative: QUERETARO, Mexico — President Claudia Sheinbaum said Mexico will never accept foreign interference or return to being a colony during a ceremony marking the 109th anniversary of the Constitution. "Mexico does not bow, does not kneel, does not surrender and is not for sale," Sheinbaum stated before representatives of other government branches. She criticized the neoliberal period's privatizations and said recent constitutional reforms have restored the document's social character. Queretaro Governor Mauricio Kuri expressed support for Sheinbaum, saying "Mexico does not accept foreign dictates" and the president "is not alone."

main_stories.title: Mexico, US sign critical minerals supply chain agreement
main_stories.narrative: MEXICO CITY, Mexico — Mexico and the United States signed an action plan to protect critical mineral supply chains, officials said. Jamieson Greer, head of the U.S. Trade Representative's Office, called the agreement "pioneering" and said it strengthens commercial ties between the neighboring countries ahead of the USMCA review in 2026. The governments will work over the next 60 days to identify specific critical minerals of common interest and design coordinated trade policies to mitigate supply chain risks from extraction to advanced manufacturing. The plan includes exploring price floors for critical mineral imports to counter dumping practices or hidden subsidies.

main_stories.title: Sheinbaum defends Supreme Court chief after shoe-cleaning video
main_stories.narrative: MEXICO CITY, Mexico — President Claudia Sheinbaum defended Supreme Court Chief Justice Hugo Aguilar after a viral video showed staff members cleaning his shoes, saying his public apology was appropriate. Speaking at her Friday morning press conference at the 12th Infantry Battalion, Sheinbaum said "it would have been bad if he hadn't said anything" and praised Aguilar for explaining that staff cleaned coffee and cream stains from his shoes. She said the controversy stems from opposition to recent judicial reforms rather than the incident itself.

international_stories.title: Mexico's Sheinbaum Opens Train Line, Addresses BTS Concert Issues
international_stories.narrative: MEXICO CITY, Mexico — President Claudia Sheinbaum inaugurated the Mexico City-Toluca train line Monday and announced government action against Ticketmaster over BTS concert ticket sales. Consumer protection agency Profeco said it initiated proceedings to fine Ticketmaster more than 5 million pesos for alleged law violations in selling tickets for the K-pop group's concerts. Sheinbaum said South Korea's government responded to her letter requesting additional BTS concert dates, with officials contacting the band's production company to evaluate the request. The president also criticized legislators during her morning press conference for prioritizing photo opportunities over serving constituents during her recent visit to San Quintín, Baja California.

international_stories.title: Opposition Governor Backs Sheinbaum Amid Foreign Pressure
international_stories.narrative: QUERETARO, Mexico — Opposition Governor Mauricio Kuri called for unified support behind President Claudia Sheinbaum during a Constitution Day ceremony, saying Mexico faces foreign pressure. "Mexico does not accept foreign dictates, does not admit instructions from anyone," the National Action Party governor said at the Teatro de la República. Kuri urged consensus on electoral reform, stating it should strengthen rather than divide democracy. Senate President Laura Itzel Castillo praised Sheinbaum's diplomatic leadership amid international challenges.

international_stories.title: Sheinbaum calls on US to stop arms trafficking to Mexico
international_stories.narrative: MEXICO CITY, Mexico — President Claudia Sheinbaum on Wednesday reiterated her call for the United States to halt arms trafficking to Mexico and rejected as "absolutely false" claims by U.S. President Donald Trump that cartels govern the country. Sheinbaum said at her regular press conference that bilateral security cooperation must be based on shared responsibility and respect for sovereignty. She stated that at least 75 percent of high-powered weapons seized in Mexico come illegally from the United States, emphasizing that just as Mexico works to prevent fentanyl from reaching the U.S., it is essential for the U.S. to control arms entering Mexico.

international_stories.title: Sheinbaum says Mexico will cooperate in Epstein investigation if requested
international_stories.narrative: MEXICO CITY, Mexico — President Claudia Sheinbaum said Wednesday that Mexico will participate in investigations related to Jeffrey Epstein files if the U.S. Department of Justice formally requests collaboration. "It is an investigation in the United States. If the Department of Justice requests Mexico's collaboration we will participate, but it is an investigation that occurs in the United States," Sheinbaum said during her press conference. Her comments came amid renewed public attention on documents linked to Epstein, who led a sexual exploitation network of minors and died in prison in 2019 while facing federal charges. Recently released judicial files have mentioned names of Mexican businessmen including Carlos Slim, María Asunción Aramburuzabala and Paula Cussi, though authorities have noted that being mentioned in the files does not mean individuals committed crimes.

international_stories.title: Family seeks Sheinbaum intervention for missing engineer in Sinaloa
international_stories.narrative: MEXICO CITY, Mexico — The family of a missing 26-year-old engineer has requested President Claudia Sheinbaum's intervention to help locate their son, who disappeared Jan. 23 in Sinaloa state. Pablo Osorio Sánchez, a civil engineer from Oaxaca working on a mining project linked to Canadian company Vizsla Silver Corp, vanished along with about 10 other mining sector workers near La Concordia municipality, his mother Socorro Osorio said. The UN Committee on Enforced Disappearances has issued an urgent action for the case, according to the family's lawyer. Osorio's mother made a direct appeal to Sheinbaum, saying "I want them to support me in searching for my son, through the president."

domestic_stories.title: Mexican youths tattoo president's drawings, video goes viral
domestic_stories.narrative: MEXICO CITY, Mexico — Two young people received permanent tattoos based on heart drawings that President Claudia Sheinbaum had sketched on their arms, according to a viral TikTok video. The video, posted by user Astrid C. González, shows Sheinbaum expressing surprise when told about the tattoos, responding "No, qué bárbaras!" ("No, how crazy!"), according to the social media post. The tattoos feature simple hearts with the words "amor" (love) and "con amor" (with love), based on drawings Sheinbaum had made for the young women during a previous encounter, González said. The video accumulated more than one million views on the platform, González said.

domestic_stories.title: Morena leader says Campeche dispute affects Sheinbaum presidency
domestic_stories.narrative: MEXICO CITY, Mexico — The confrontation between Campeche Governor Layda Sansores and the state legislature affects President Claudia Sheinbaum and internal party unity, said Ricardo Monreal Ávila, coordinator of Morena deputies in the federal Congress. Monreal said the dispute between officials from the same party creates a "confrontation that affects the movement we belong to" after Campeche legislators voted in private session to restore constitutional immunity amid what they called political persecution by Sansores. The Morena leader said such internal conflicts "affect President Sheinbaum and the movement" ahead of next year's elections in Campeche for governor, mayors and legislators.

domestic_stories.title: Sheinbaum says electoral reform will surprise critics
domestic_stories.narrative: MEXICO CITY, Mexico — President Claudia Sheinbaum said her upcoming electoral reform proposal will surprise critics who have condemned the initiative before seeing its contents. Sheinbaum said the reform is progressing well and will be presented this month, according to comments made during her daily press conference. She criticized opposition figures who signed a statement calling the reform a threat to democracy, noting the document criticizes an initiative "that is not yet known." Sheinbaum said she has not proposed removing autonomy from the National Electoral Institute, as opponents claim.

domestic_stories.title: PRI loses third of members in two years
domestic_stories.narrative: MEXICO CITY, Mexico — Mexico's Institutional Revolutionary Party has lost one-third of its members over the past two years, according to party records. The PRI, which governed Mexico for seven decades until 2000, has seen its membership decline significantly during the current period.

domestic_stories.title: Mexico's Pemex announces $21 billion investment plan for 2026
domestic_stories.narrative: MEXICO CITY, Mexico — Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum announced a 425 billion peso ($21 billion) investment plan for state oil company Pemex during her morning press conference, according to company director Víctor Rodríguez. The investments aim to increase oil production to 1.8 million barrels daily and natural gas output to 4.5 billion cubic feet daily by 2026, Rodríguez said. The plan includes modernizing refineries in Tula and Salina Cruz to process 1.56 million barrels daily and boosting ammonia production for fertilizers to 560,000 tons annually, he said. Energy Secretary Luz Elena González said Pemex reduced its debt by 20% in 2025, reaching its lowest financial debt level in 11 years.

domestic_stories.title: Sheinbaum names General Briceño as new National Guard commander
domestic_stories.narrative: MORELIA, Mexico — President Claudia Sheinbaum announced Friday that General Guillermo Briceño will serve as the new commander of Mexico's National Guard, replacing General Hernán Cortés. Sheinbaum said during her morning press conference that Cortés will assume a new position as chief officer in the Defense Ministry. The president made the announcement at the 12th Infantry Battalion of the 21st Military Zone, where she asked Briceño to stand so attendees could meet him.

domestic_stories.title: Human Rights Watch says AMLO caused democratic backsliding in Mexico
domestic_stories.narrative: MEXICO CITY, Mexico — Human Rights Watch said former President Andrés Manuel López Obrador led Mexico into democratic backsliding that undermined judicial independence, transparency and rule of law, according to the organization's World Report 2026. The report said President Claudia Sheinbaum, who became Mexico's first female president in October 2024, inherited severe human rights problems including extreme criminal violence and serious military abuses. Human Rights Watch stated that with Sheinbaum's backing, Congress approved a judicial reform in September 2024 requiring all judges to stand for election, with the first elections held June 1. The organization reported Mexico's official homicide rate in 2024 exceeded 25 per 100,000 inhabitants, among the world's highest.

domestic_stories.title: Sheinbaum announces scholarships at new university campus opening
domestic_stories.narrative: SAN LUIS POTOSI, Mexico — President Claudia Sheinbaum announced that all students in the Rosario Castellanos University system will receive the Gertrudis Bocanegra scholarship during the inauguration of the university's first campus phase in San Luis Potosi. The scholarship provides 1,900 pesos bimonthly for transportation and other expenses for up to 45 months, Sheinbaum said. She criticized previous neoliberal policies for treating education as a business rather than a constitutional right. Governor Ricardo Gallardo said the new campus will offer programs in robotics, artificial intelligence and electronics to meet automotive industry demand.

main_stories.title: Ukraine brings home 157 from Russian captivity in swap
main_stories.narrative: KYIV, Ukraine — Ukraine returned 157 of its citizens from Russian captivity in the latest prisoner exchange, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said. The swap resulted from trilateral peace talks held in Abu Dhabi, the capital of the United Arab Emirates, Zelenskyy confirmed. Ukrainian delegates Rustem Umierov, Kyrylo Budanov, and Davyd Arakhamiia participated in the negotiations with Russian and American delegations, with talks expected to continue. Zelenskyy said in January that Russia had halted prisoner exchanges because it did not believe it gained from them.

main_stories.title: Zelenskyy says full Donbas occupation would cost Russia 800,000 soldiers
main_stories.narrative: KYIV, Ukraine — Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Russia would need at least two years and suffer 800,000 military deaths to fully occupy eastern Ukraine's Donbas Oblast, according to an interview with French broadcaster France 2 reported by Le Monde. "Russia wants us to leave the entire Donbas Oblast. Since the beginning of this war, they have not won a single victory," Zelenskyy said. The president said even maintaining Ukraine's current positions under a potential conflict freeze would represent "a significant concession" by Ukraine. Zelenskyy added that Russians "need a break" and said Ukraine must have control over its part of any demilitarized zone.

international_stories.title: Zelenskyy, NATO Chief Honor Fallen Ukrainian Warriors in Kyiv
international_stories.narrative: KYIV, Ukraine — President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte honored fallen Ukrainian warriors at a memorial ceremony in the capital, the president's office said. The leaders placed memorial candles and paid tribute to Ukrainian defenders at the People's Memorial of National Remembrance at Maidan Nezalezhnosti during Rutte's visit to Ukraine. The ceremony took place at the central square that served as the focal point of Ukraine's 2014 pro-European protests.

international_stories.title: Zelenskyy says Russia offered US $12 trillion cooperation package
international_stories.narrative: KYIV, Ukraine — Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Russia has offered the United States an economic cooperation package worth about $12 trillion, according to Ukrainian intelligence briefings. Zelenskyy said at a press conference that the proposal, which he called the "Dmitriev package," involves economic cooperation between Russia and the US, Ukrinform reported. He said Ukraine would not support any arrangements about Ukraine without Ukraine's participation, stating that any clauses relating to Ukraine in potential US-Russia bilateral agreements could not contradict Ukraine's Constitution or laws. Zelenskyy said Ukraine "will show its reaction if such risks arise."

international_stories.title: Zelenskyy says Putin fears Trump but not Europeans
international_stories.narrative: KYIV, Ukraine — Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Russian leader Vladimir Putin fears U.S. President Donald Trump but is not afraid of European leaders, according to an interview with France 2 reported by Le Monde. "Putin is only afraid of Trump, that's a fact," Zelenskyy said, adding that Trump "wants to end this war with compromises" but warned there "can be no compromise when it comes to our sovereignty." Zelenskyy said Putin "is only looking to humiliate Europe" and criticized efforts by French President Emmanuel Macron to restore dialogue with Putin, saying pressure on the Russian leader is "not enough."

domestic_stories.title: Zelenskyy Honors State Special Transport Service Members with Awards
domestic_stories.narrative: KYIV, Ukraine — President Volodymyr Zelenskyy honored servicemembers of the State Special Transport Service with military decorations on their professional holiday, according to the presidential office. Zelenskyy said the service members carry out combat missions and thanked them for strengthening Ukraine's defense forces and fighting against enemy forces. The president awarded the Order "For Courage," the Order of Princess Olga, and the Order of Danylo Halytskyi to the servicemembers. Zelenskyy said on behalf of the Ukrainian people he thanked the defenders and their fellow service members for their work.

between_the_lines: Zelenskyy's public statements this week reveal a strategic shift toward framing Ukraine's military position in specific, quantifiable terms—citing exact casualty projections and timeline estimates—suggesting an effort to influence international perceptions of the conflict's sustainability.

The Ukrainian president's emphasis on distinguishing between Trump's influence over Putin versus European leaders' lack thereof indicates Ukraine is recalibrating its diplomatic messaging to align with the new U.S. administration's approach to Russia.

Despite ongoing prisoner exchanges and ceremonial activities, Zelenskyy's focus on Russia's alleged $12 trillion economic offer to the U.S. suggests Ukraine is increasingly concerned about potential bilateral arrangements that could bypass Ukrainian interests.
leader_dossiers.executive_summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy accused Russia this week of breaking a promised pause in energy infrastructure strikes, while announcing a prisoner exchange that brought home 157 Ukrainians from Russian captivity. Zelenskyy said Russia offered the United States a $12 trillion cooperation package and claimed full occupation of the Donbas region would cost Russia 800,000 soldiers. The Ukrainian leader also stated that Russian President Vladimir Putin fears former President Donald Trump but not European leaders.

main_stories.title: Vance meets Italian PM Meloni during Milan Olympics visit
main_stories.narrative: MILAN, Italy — Vice President JD Vance met Friday with Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni during his weeklong visit to Italy for the Winter Olympics, according to the vice president's office. The hour-long meeting at the Prefettura di Milano was followed by a closed-door lunch, with only brief remarks open to the press. Vance's office said the leaders discussed bilateral relations, the Olympics and efforts to improve business and investment climate between the nations. Vance also attended the Olympics opening ceremony at San Siro Stadium with Secretary of State Marco Rubio.

main_stories.title: Vatican Orders Removal of Meloni Face from Church Fresco
main_stories.narrative: ROME, Italy — The Vatican ordered the removal of Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni's face from a church fresco after it sparked controversy, according to the restorer who painted it. Bruno Valentinetti, 83, said he covered the face in the San Lorenzo in Lucina basilica "because the Vatican asked me to." The fresco had drawn crowds and criticism after Valentinetti painted what appeared to be Meloni's likeness on an angel figure during restoration work. Rome's vicariate said sacred art "cannot be subject to improper use or exploitation."

main_stories.title: Meloni calls Olympics protesters 'enemies of Italy'
main_stories.narrative: ROME, Italy — Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni called protesters who demonstrated against the Milan-Cortina 2026 Olympics "enemies of Italy and Italians" following clashes with police in Milan. "Thousands and thousands of Italians are working so that everything functions during the Olympics," Meloni said in a social media post Sunday. The prime minister condemned what she called "gangs of delinquents" after about 5,000 protesters marched through Milan, with some throwing stones at police near the Olympic Village area. Defense Minister Guido Crosetto and other government officials also condemned the violence, expressing solidarity with law enforcement.

main_stories.title: Meloni approves security decree, criticizes magistrates over protesters
main_stories.narrative: ROME, Italy — Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni's government approved a security decree Thursday that includes preventive detention powers and legal protections for police officers, Interior Minister Matteo Piantedosi said. Meloni criticized magistrates for releasing three protesters involved in violent clashes in Turin, calling it a "double standard" by certain parts of the judiciary, she said during a television interview. The decree allows 12-hour preventive detention for troublemakers and restricts knife sales to minors, Justice Minister Carlo Nordio said. The measures take effect immediately and will apply during the upcoming Milan-Cortina Olympics, Piantedosi said.

main_stories.title: Meloni backs comedian who quit Sanremo over criticism
main_stories.narrative: ROME, Italy — Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni expressed solidarity with comedian Andrea Pucci after he withdrew from co-hosting Italy's Sanremo music festival following criticism and threats. Pucci said he received "incomprehensible and unacceptable" insults and threats against his family after his selection was announced. Meloni called the situation a "frightening illiberal drift of the left" on Facebook, while Deputy Prime Minister Matteo Salvini also voiced support for the comedian.

international_stories.title: Italian PM Meloni meets Polish President in Milan
international_stories.narrative: MILAN, Italy — Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni met with Polish President Karol Nawrocki in Milan on Tuesday to discuss bilateral relations and international issues, according to the Italian government. The leaders discussed economic cooperation and defense industry collaboration, the government said. Both leaders emphasized their shared commitment to supporting Ukraine's path toward peace and stressed the importance of strengthening transatlantic relationships, according to the statement.

international_stories.title: Meloni discusses cooperation, migration with Algerian president
international_stories.narrative: ROME, Italy — Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni held a telephone conversation with Algerian President Abdelmadjid Tebboune to discuss bilateral relations and cooperation initiatives, the Italian government said. The leaders reviewed progress on joint projects under Italy's Mattei Plan, including an agricultural training center in Sidi Bel Abbes and desert farming initiatives, according to the government statement. They also discussed migration cooperation and efforts to combat human trafficking. Tebboune extended an invitation for Meloni to visit Algeria, which she accepted, the government said.

international_stories.title: Meloni meets Chilean president-elect at Rome palace
international_stories.narrative: ROME, Italy — Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni met with Chilean President-elect José Antonio Kast at Palazzo Chigi, congratulating him on his recent electoral victory ahead of his upcoming inauguration, the Italian government said. Kast outlined his future government's priorities, including measures to boost economic growth, attract investment, strengthen crime fighting and support birth rates, according to the statement. The two leaders agreed to broaden bilateral cooperation in these areas and intensify dialogue with Latin American partners on strategic sectors to strengthen supply chains for energy and critical raw materials.

international_stories.title: Germany considers joining Italy-UK-Japan fighter jet program
international_stories.narrative: ROME, Italy — German Chancellor Friedrich Merz discussed potential German participation in the GCAP sixth-generation fighter jet program during talks with Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni, according to high-level German and Italian sources. The sources said Meloni expressed openness to German involvement in the joint venture between Italy's Leonardo, Britain's BAE Systems and Japan's Mitsubishi. The development comes as Germany weighs withdrawing from the competing Franco-German FCAS fighter program amid reported disputes between French company Dassault and European aerospace giant Airbus. A German Foreign Ministry official said Berlin must 'close well' with Paris on any separation from the FCAS project.

domestic_stories.title: Meloni faces political crossroads after Vannacci breaks from coalition
domestic_stories.narrative: ROME, Italy — Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni confronts a strategic dilemma following General Roberto Vannacci's departure from the League party to form his own movement, according to Italian political analysts. Political risk analyst Fulvio Lorefice of Bistoncini Partners said the move could force a shift toward radicalization that might undermine Meloni's efforts to court moderate voters. Lorefice stated that pursuing Vannacci's hardline positions on immigration and security could damage Meloni's political investment in centrist Catholic organizations. The development raises questions about whether Italy's right-wing coalition will move toward the political center or embrace more extreme positions.

domestic_stories.title: Brothers of Italy office vandalized in Meloni's Rome district
domestic_stories.narrative: ROME, Italy — Vandals defaced a Brothers of Italy party office overnight in the Garbatella district where Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni grew up, party officials said Thursday. The attackers spray-painted a hammer and sickle symbol and anti-fascist graffiti on the shutters of the office, according to FdI lawmakers Paolo Trancassini and Marco Perissa. The party coordinators condemned what they called a "cowardly act of vandalism" and blamed "a climate of hatred fuelled by a part of the Left" for the incident.

domestic_stories.title: Meloni calls Turin social center clashes attempted murder
domestic_stories.narrative: TURIN, Italy — Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni said clashes during the eviction of a social center in Turin constituted attempted murder after visiting two hospitalized police officers. Meloni said the officers, ages 28 and 29, were attacked with hammers, Molotov cocktails and nail-filled bombs during yesterday's confrontation at the Askatasuna social center. "These are not protesters; these are organised criminals," Meloni said, calling for judicial action and announcing a government meeting to discuss new security measures. The prime minister said attackers used communication jammers and various weapons against law enforcement during the eviction operation.

domestic_stories.title: Italian columnist analyzes Meloni's political durability versus Renzi's downfall
domestic_stories.narrative: MILAN, Italy — A political columnist for Corriere della Sera analyzed Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni's political resilience compared to former Prime Minister Matteo Renzi's political collapse in a reader response published by the Italian newspaper. The columnist, identified as Aldo, said Meloni has been "more prudent" and benefits from operating within the stronger center-right political coalition. He attributed Renzi's downfall to being "too left for the right, and too right for the left," facing internal party opposition and judicial pressure on his family. The analysis questioned how long Meloni's appeal to voters will last amid Italy's economic challenges.

between_the_lines: Meloni is simultaneously engaging in high-level international diplomacy while facing domestic security challenges, as evidenced by her meetings with foreign leaders occurring alongside protests, vandalism of party offices, and the need for new security legislation.

The Vatican's intervention to remove Meloni's face from a church fresco suggests potential tensions between Italy's conservative government and Catholic Church leadership over appropriate boundaries between religious and political imagery.

Meloni's coalition faces internal strain with General Vannacci's departure from the League to form his own movement, creating a strategic challenge for maintaining parliamentary unity while the government pushes through controversial security measures.

The Prime Minister's public support for comedian Andrea Pucci after his Sanremo withdrawal indicates Meloni is actively defending cultural figures aligned with her political base against what she frames as ideological pressure.
leader_dossiers.executive_summary: Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni conducted extensive international diplomacy this week, meeting with U.S. Vice President-elect J.D. Vance, Polish President Andrzej Duda, and leaders from Algeria and Chile amid Italy's hosting of Olympic events in Milan. The Vatican ordered the removal of Meloni's face from a church fresco, while domestically she approved new security legislation and criticized magistrates over handling of protesters she called 'enemies of Italy.' Her governing coalition faced strain as General Roberto Vannacci left the League party to form his own political movement, creating potential challenges for parliamentary unity.

main_stories.title: Finland's Stubb says US ideology conflicts with Finnish values
main_stories.narrative: HELSINKI, Finland — Finnish President Alexander Stubb said Wednesday that the current U.S. administration's foreign policy is guided by an ideology that conflicts with Finnish values, citing America's undermining of international institutions and diminished focus on Europe. Speaking at the opening of Parliament, Stubb said Finland must acknowledge that the United States is changing in its approach to allies and foreign policy, though he called the U.S. an important ally. Stubb said the administration's 'Make America Great Again' ideology downplays the international rules-based order and the European Union, areas where Finland disagrees with Washington. Finland will update its foreign and security policy doctrine to reflect changes in the international situation, Stubb told lawmakers.

main_stories.title: Finnish President to Attend Milan Winter Olympics Opening Ceremony
main_stories.narrative: HELSINKI, Finland — Finnish President Alexander Stubb will attend the opening ceremony of the 2026 Winter Olympics in Milan on Feb. 6, the president's office said Sunday. Stubb and his wife Suzanne Innes-Stubb will participate in a reception at Palazzo Reale hosted by Italian President Sergio Mattarella and the official opening ceremony at San Siro stadium in Milan, according to a press release. The 2026 Winter Olympics will be held in Milan and Cortina d'Ampezzo, Italy, from Feb. 6-22.

main_stories.title: Finnish President Stubb visits schools, businesses in Vantaa
main_stories.narrative: VANTAA, Finland — President Alexander Stubb and his spouse Suzanne Innes-Stubb visited the city of Vantaa on Tuesday, touring educational institutions and local businesses. The presidential couple began at Lehtikuusen koulu comprehensive school, where first-grade pupils welcomed them and conducted interviews about language learning, according to the Office of the President. They later visited Vantaa Vocational College Varia's aircraft maintenance programs and Sensofusion, a drone-detection technology company that received the President's Internationalisation Award in 2025. "Vantaa is Finland's most international and multicultural city," Stubb said during a public event at Jumbo shopping centre.

between_the_lines: Stubb's criticism of U.S. foreign policy ideology represents a notable departure from Finland's traditionally careful diplomatic language regarding major allies, suggesting a more assertive presidential communication style.

The president's domestic travel schedule to Kouvola and Vantaa indicates a focus on regional engagement and visibility outside the capital, potentially building political capital through direct citizen contact.

Stubb's planned attendance at the 2026 Milan Olympics opening ceremony demonstrates Finland's continued emphasis on international sporting diplomacy and maintaining strong European ties amid broader geopolitical tensions.
leader_dossiers.executive_summary: Finnish President Alexander Stubb said this week that U.S. ideology conflicts with Finnish values, marking a departure from Finland's typically measured diplomatic language toward major allies. Stubb maintained an active domestic schedule with visits to schools and businesses in Vantaa and a planned trip to Kouvola, while also confirming his attendance at the 2026 Milan Winter Olympics opening ceremony. The president's statements and travel schedule reflect both a more assertive communication style on foreign policy and continued emphasis on domestic engagement and European partnerships.

main_stories.title: Lithuania president vows to push for Belarus sanctions extension
main_stories.narrative: VILNIUS, Lithuania — Lithuanian President Gitanas Nausėda said Tuesday he will push firmly for the European Union to extend sanctions on Belarus when the bloc decides in late February. "I will be among those who most firmly demand the extension of these sanctions," Nausėda told Žinių Radijas radio. He cited Belarus's continued alignment with Russia, imprisonment of political prisoners and what he described as hybrid attacks using smuggling balloons that have repeatedly forced temporary suspensions at Vilnius Airport. The most recent balloon incident occurred last week, prompting what Nausėda said was a strong U.S. response warning Minsk that such actions could undermine efforts to improve bilateral relations.

main_stories.title: Lithuanian authorities to inspect president's property over land complaint
main_stories.narrative: VILNIUS, Lithuania — Lithuania's State Territorial Planning and Construction Inspectorate will inspect President Gitanas Nausėda's private residence in February following a complaint alleging he may have unlawfully occupied state-owned land, the Delfi.lt news portal reported Thursday. The inspection concerns Nausėda's home in Pavilniai Regional Park, where he has continued to live instead of moving to the official presidential residence in Turniškės after taking office. The Presidential Office told Delfi.lt that Nausėda is aware of the planned inspection and said it is up to authorities to determine whether the complaint is well-founded.

international_stories.title: Lithuanian President Calls for Investigation into Epstein Files
international_stories.narrative: VILNIUS, Lithuania — President Gitanas Nausėda called on Lithuanian law enforcement to thoroughly examine communications from deceased U.S. financier and sex offender Jeffrey Epstein that mention Lithuanians, according to an interview broadcast Tuesday on Žinių radio. Nausėda said authorities should use legal assistance agreements with the United States if needed to investigate the matter. "I hope that institutions will evaluate in principle what they receive," Nausėda said, adding that while much information has been redacted, Lithuania has a legal assistance treaty with the U.S. The president said the available information "raises, to put it mildly, quite a few doubts."

domestic_stories.title: Lithuanian President warns about Remigijus Žemaitaitis ties
domestic_stories.narrative: VILNIUS, Lithuania — President Gitanas Nausėda said Tuesday he sees a "serious problem" with connections between Nemuno Aušra party chairman Remigijus Žemaitaitis and party representatives with A. Perminas. "There is even a possible shadow of criminalization that must be denied," Nausėda said in an interview with Žinių radijas. The president warned that if Žemaitaitis continues to follow the coalition "like a shadow," it could undermine all the coalition's good work.

domestic_stories.title: Poll shows majority of Lithuanians view president negatively
domestic_stories.narrative: VILNIUS, Lithuania — More than half of Lithuanians said their opinion of President Gitanas Nausėda had worsened last year, according to a survey published by public broadcaster LRT. The poll showed 54% of respondents reported a more negative view of the president, while only 5% said their opinion had improved, according to pollster Baltijos tyrimai. The survey of 1,063 adults was conducted from Jan. 8-24 with a margin of error of up to 3.1%. Men, people over 50, rural residents, managers and the unemployed were more likely to report worsened views of Nausėda, the poll said.

between_the_lines: Nausėda faces mounting domestic scrutiny across multiple fronts simultaneously - from property inspections to declining public approval - while maintaining an active international stance on Belarus sanctions.
The president's call for investigation into Epstein files mentioning Lithuania suggests potential concerns about the country's international reputation amid other controversies.
The convergence of a property complaint investigation and majority negative polling indicates Nausėda's political standing may be increasingly vulnerable to both legal and public opinion pressures.
Nausėda's warnings about political party connections to external influences, combined with his Belarus sanctions push, reflect ongoing concerns about foreign interference in Lithuanian politics.
leader_dossiers.executive_summary: Lithuanian President Gitanas Nausėda faced mounting domestic challenges this week as authorities announced an inspection of his property following a land complaint and polling showed a majority of Lithuanians view him negatively. Despite the scrutiny, Nausėda maintained his international focus, vowing to push for extended sanctions against Belarus and calling for an investigation into Epstein files that mention Lithuania. The convergence of legal oversight, declining public approval, and the president's warnings about political figure Remigijus Žemaitaitis highlighted a week of simultaneous pressures on multiple fronts.

main_stories.title: Moldova's Sandu nominated for Nobel Peace Prize
main_stories.narrative: CHISINAU, Moldova — Moldovan President Maia Sandu said Thursday she was nominated for the Nobel Peace Prize but stated that Ukrainians deserve the award instead. Norwegian parliamentarian Arild Hermstad nominated Sandu for her efforts to defend democracy against Russian influence attempts, including cyberattacks, disinformation and political pressure, according to the nomination. Sandu made her comments during a TV8 program on the same day Ukraine conducted a prisoner exchange with Russia involving 157 people from each side.

main_stories.title: Moldova President Meets Baltic Parliament Leaders on EU Integration
main_stories.narrative: CHISINAU, Moldova — President Maia Sandu met with the parliamentary speakers of Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania to discuss Moldova's European Union integration process, the presidency said. The meeting with Estonian Riigikogu President Lauri Hussar, Latvian Saeima President Daiga Mieriņa and Lithuanian Seimas President Juozas Olekas marked the first joint official visit by all three Baltic legislative leaders to Moldova. Sandu cited economic data showing the Baltic states' success after EU membership, with Lithuania seeing average gross salaries increase nearly seven-fold and GDP per capita grow four-fold since joining the bloc. The leaders also discussed regional security and ways to counter hybrid warfare threats, including cyberattacks and disinformation campaigns.

main_stories.title: Maia Sandu proposes consultations for protecting children in the online environment
main_stories.narrative: Maia Sandu proposes consultations for protecting children in the online environment

international_stories.title: Moldova Foreign Minister Open to Creative EU Membership Ideas
international_stories.narrative: CHISINAU, Moldova — Moldova's Foreign Minister Mihai Popșoi said the country is open to "creative ideas" that could accelerate European Union membership, even if it means initially joining without full member rights. Popșoi told Euroactiv that obtaining tangible progress before the 2028 presidential elections is essential for maintaining public support. His comments follow reports that Brussels is considering allowing candidate countries to join the EU without full voting rights initially. President Maia Sandu previously stated that Moldova seeks full EU membership rights and does not want shortcuts in the accession process.

international_stories.title: Moldova's Sandu says incomes higher despite Ukraine war impact
international_stories.narrative: CHISINAU, Moldova — President Maia Sandu said most Moldovan citizens now earn higher incomes than in previous years, even accounting for inflation, though economic growth remains constrained by the war in Ukraine. Speaking on TV8's "Cutia Neagra" program Feb. 5, Sandu said pension increases and salary growth could have been larger without the economic disruption from the neighboring conflict. She said the Ukraine war continues to create "major uncertainty for investors" and affects the country's economic development, though political stability after recent elections has provided some positive signals.

international_stories.title: Moldova's Sandu defends social media regulation against US report
international_stories.narrative: CHISINAU, Moldova — President Maia Sandu said freedom of expression applies to people, not fake accounts, responding to a U.S. House Judiciary Committee report suggesting the European Union pressured social media platforms to censor content during elections in several countries including Moldova. "Freedom of expression is for people, not for fake accounts, not for bots," Sandu said during a Feb. 5 television interview on TV8. The interim report published Feb. 3 alleged EU institutions created pressure mechanisms on social networks to moderate political discourse, potentially influencing elections. Sandu said Moldova has evidence of fake account operations and defended the need for platform regulation.

international_stories.title: Moldovan Socialist Deputy Explains Why He Didn't Applaud Sandu Speech
international_stories.narrative: CHISINAU, Moldova — Socialist deputy Igor Dodon said he refused to applaud or stand during President Maia Sandu's speech to the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe because he disagreed with her message. Dodon said at a Feb. 2 press conference that Sandu's Jan. 27 address was "geopolitical" and focused on "frustrations" about Russia and the war in Ukraine. Sandu had told the assembly that Europe faces two Russian-initiated wars and that Moldova is on the front line of Russian hybrid aggression. Other officials in attendance gave Sandu a standing ovation.

domestic_stories.title: Moldova President Says Special Envoys Work Without Pay
domestic_stories.narrative: CHISINAU, Moldova — President Maia Sandu said her special envoys Nicu Popescu and Dorin Recean work without salaries or offices, serving as unpaid advisers on resilience and hybrid warfare issues. Sandu stated during a TV8 interview that she calls on them when their expertise is needed and they represent Moldova in forums discussing resilience. Former Prime Minister Recean was appointed special envoy for development and resilience in December, while former Foreign Minister Popescu became special envoy for European affairs and strategic partnerships in October.

domestic_stories.title: Sandu says former health minister chose to leave government
domestic_stories.narrative: CHISINAU, Moldova — President Maia Sandu said former Health Minister Ala Nemerenco chose not to continue working in state institutions after her mandate expired, according to statements made during a Feb. 5 television interview. Sandu said she had discussions with Nemerenco but declined to provide details, stating that "each person decided for themselves what they want to do next." Nemerenco previously said in December that she perceived receiving the Order of the Republic as a signal of departure and that no clear proposal was made for her to remain in the new government led by Prime Minister Alexandru Munteanu.

between_the_lines: Sandu is actively managing Moldova's international image through strategic messaging, deflecting Nobel Prize attention to Ukraine while simultaneously defending against U.S. criticism of social media policies.

The president appears to be restructuring her advisory network with unpaid special envoys handling sensitive security issues, suggesting either budget constraints or a desire for more flexible, less formal arrangements.

Despite claiming economic progress for citizens, Sandu faces visible domestic political opposition, as evidenced by Socialist deputy Dodon's public refusal to show respect during her international speeches.

Moldova's EU integration strategy is becoming more pragmatic, with officials openly discussing 'creative ideas' for partial membership while Sandu maintains intensive diplomatic engagement with Baltic allies.
leader_dossiers.executive_summary: Moldova President Maia Sandu was nominated for the Nobel Peace Prize this week while meeting with Baltic Parliament leaders to discuss EU integration efforts. Sandu defended her administration's social media regulations against criticism in a U.S. report and announced that special envoys working on security issues serve without government pay. The president also stated that incomes have increased despite economic pressures from the ongoing war in neighboring Ukraine.

main_stories.title: Brazil's Lula launches national pact against femicide
main_stories.narrative: BRASILIA, Brazil — President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva launched a national pact Wednesday to combat femicide, bringing together Brazil's executive, legislative and judicial branches to address lethal violence against women. The agreement establishes integrated actions for prevention, protection, accountability of aggressors and rights guarantees, according to the presidential palace. Women's Minister Márcia Lopes joined Lula at the ceremony in the Planalto Palace's Noble Hall. In December, Lula said he decided to assume responsibility for creating "a kind of movement that could become a pact against femicide, against violence against women."

main_stories.title: Lula visits Salvador to deliver health equipment
main_stories.narrative: SALVADOR, Brazil — President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva traveled to Salvador on Friday for official engagements including a health equipment delivery ceremony. The presidential delegation departed Brasília at 8 a.m. and arrived in the Bahian capital at 9:35 a.m., according to official scheduling. At 11:30 a.m., Lula participated in a ceremony delivering ambulances and health equipment under the New PAC Health program, followed by a 4 p.m. visit to the Irmã Dulce Social Works.

main_stories.title: Lula says Master Bank case will be investigated thoroughly
main_stories.narrative: BRASÍLIA, Brazil — President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva said Thursday that the Master Bank case will be investigated thoroughly without political interference, confirming he met with bank owner Daniel Vorcaro in November 2024. Lula told UOL news portal that he assured Vorcaro there would be no political position for or against Master Bank, only technical investigation by the Central Bank. The president said the case represents an extraordinary chance to catch corruption and money laundering magnates, calling it potentially the country's biggest economic scandal. Master Bank was liquidated by Brazil's Central Bank in November following Federal Police investigations into alleged financial fraud.

main_stories.title: Brazil's Lula considers economist for Central Bank directorship
main_stories.narrative: BRASÍLIA, Brazil — President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva is considering appointing Guilherme Mello, the Finance Ministry's economic policy secretary, to a vacant Central Bank directorship, Finance Minister Fernando Haddad said this week. Mello said Friday he has not received a formal invitation but would be honored to serve if asked. Market analysts expressed concern that Mello's developmentalist economic views, which favor faster interest rate cuts, could undermine the Central Bank's inflation-fighting credibility. Two Central Bank directorships became vacant at the start of this year when the last directors appointed by former President Jair Bolsonaro completed their terms.

main_stories.title: Lula Delivers Speech at 2026 Judicial Year Opening
main_stories.narrative: BRASÍLIA, Brazil — President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva delivered a speech at the opening ceremony of the 2026 Judicial Year, according to official Planalto Palace records. The event marked the formal beginning of the Brazilian judiciary's annual calendar. Details of the president's remarks were not immediately available.

international_stories.title: Lula calls US pressure on Cuba 'massacre of speculation'
international_stories.narrative: SALVADOR, Brazil — President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva said Cuba suffers from a 'massacre of speculation' caused by the United States and defended internal solutions for Venezuela's situation during a Workers' Party anniversary event. Lula said Brazil 'is solidary with the Cuban people, who are victims of a massacre of speculation by the United States against them,' according to remarks at the party's 46th anniversary celebration. The initiative aims to formalize property rights for residents in the mountainous city located north of Rio de Janeiro.

domestic_stories.title: Lula extends FGTS hospital lending program through 2030
domestic_stories.narrative: BRASÍLIA, Brazil — President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva signed a provisional measure Thursday extending a program that allows Brazil's employment fund to provide credit to philanthropic hospitals and nonprofit disability institutions through 2030. The measure, numbered 1,336, amends the 1990 law governing the Guarantee Fund for Length of Service (FGTS), according to the official text published by the presidential palace. Health Minister Alexandre Rocha Santos Padilha and Labor Minister Luiz Marinho co-signed the provisional measure, which takes immediate effect.

domestic_stories.title: Brazil purchases 2,100 vehicles for patient transport program
domestic_stories.narrative: SALVADOR, Brazil — President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva signed contracts Friday for the federal government's first purchase of 2,100 vehicles to transport public health patients needing specialized treatment away from home. The Health Ministry said the 815 million real ($135 million) investment will provide vans, minibuses and ambulances under the "Now There Are Specialists" program. Health Minister Alexandre Padilha said the initiative allows patients living 600 kilometers from capitals to receive specialist consultations at local health units instead of waiting months for referrals. The program is part of Brazil's New Health PAC infrastructure investment plan totaling 31.5 billion reais.

domestic_stories.title: Lula to veto illegal portions of congressional salary increases
domestic_stories.narrative: BRASÍLIA, Brazil — President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva will not completely veto salary increases for government employees approved by Congress this week, but will reject only provisions that violate existing legislation, according to government sources. The controversial project allows 70 employees to exceed the public service salary cap and receive extra time off for days worked. Lula's team said they are waiting for the text to reach the presidential palace so the legal affairs secretary can analyze the project, with plans to veto anything deemed illegal or unconstitutional while approving regular salary increases.

domestic_stories.title: Brazilian court rejects bid to suspend carnival funding
domestic_stories.narrative: BRASÍLIA, Brazil — A Brazilian federal audit court minister rejected a recommendation to suspend government funding to a Rio de Janeiro samba school that plans to honor President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva in its carnival parade. Minister Aroldo Cedraz said the 1 million real ($200,000) payment to Acadêmicos de Niterói follows objective criteria applied equally to all 12 schools in Rio's Special Group carnival competition. The technical staff of the Federal Court of Accounts had recommended suspending the payment following complaints from six federal deputies from the Novo party, who alleged misuse of public funds. Cedraz ordered tourism agency Embratur and other involved parties to respond to the allegations within 15 days.

domestic_stories.title: Brazil House Speaker expects Lula to approve staff raises
domestic_stories.narrative: BRASÍLIA, Brazil — House Speaker Hugo Motta said Thursday he expects President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva to approve salary increases for congressional staff that were passed by Congress this week. Motta told TV Globo that after the presidential approval, he will publish a directive increasing lawmakers' office budgets by about 30,000 reais ($5,000) monthly to cover the staff raises. The increases would raise deputies' monthly office allowances from 133,200 reais to approximately 165,000 reais, according to party leaders cited by the broadcaster.

domestic_stories.title: Brazilian courts reject challenges to Lula carnival tribute
domestic_stories.narrative: RIO DE JANEIRO, Brazil — Brazilian courts rejected legal challenges seeking to block a carnival parade honoring President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, with opponents arguing the tribute constitutes illegal early campaigning using public funds. Senator Damares Alves and Niterói city councilman Allan Lura filed separate lawsuits against the Acadêmicos de Niterói samba school's parade, which received 4 million reais in municipal funding. A federal court judge ruled the case falls outside federal jurisdiction and transferred it to district court, while a state judge in Rio de Janeiro denied an injunction request and gave authorities 15 days to respond. The Court of Auditors also recommended the federal government withhold 1 million reais in tourism funding for the parade.

The ruling halted what economists called excessive spending by Congress, which had approved salary increases and created nearly 20,000 new public positions. Alex Agostini, chief economist at Austin Rating, said the legislative package represented clear fiscal looseness that adds risk to a country already operating with extremely narrow fiscal margins. main_stories.title: Uruguay's Orsi meets Xi, signs cooperation deals in Beijing
main_stories.narrative: BEIJING, China — Uruguayan President Yamandú Orsi met with Chinese President Xi Jinping on Tuesday, signing 12 cooperation documents covering areas from trade to the environment, according to China's official Xinhua news agency. Xi said China and Uruguay should work together to advance an "equal and orderly multipolar world," while Orsi called the strategic partnership between the nations at its "best moment." Both leaders committed to starting negotiations on a free trade deal between China and the South American trade bloc Mercosur, according to a joint statement. Orsi is leading a 150-member delegation including business leaders on a visit through February 7.

international_stories.title: Uruguay's Orsi faces key challenges in 2026 roadmap
international_stories.narrative: MONTEVIDEO, Uruguay — President Yamandú Orsi faces critical challenges in 2026 including executing his first national budget, finalizing the Mercosur-European Union trade agreement, and overseeing offshore oil exploration, according to an analysis by El Observador. The newspaper identified 26 key figures who will shape Uruguay's year, with Orsi scheduled to travel to China in February to sign commercial and technological agreements. Economy Minister Gabriel Oddone will focus on reducing currency lag and achieving 2% growth through strict public spending control, the publication said.

international_stories.title: Uruguay President Orsi to attend China trade seminar
international_stories.narrative: MONTEVIDEO, Uruguay — President Yamandú Orsi will participate in a commercial promotion and investment seminar on Feb. 6, according to La Diaria. The event is organized by Uruguay XXI and the China Council for the Promotion of International Trade. The seminar aims to strengthen trade and investment ties between Uruguay and China.

international_stories.title: Businessman charged with human trafficking joins Orsi China delegation
international_stories.narrative: MONTEVIDEO, Uruguay — A businessman charged with human trafficking joined President Yamandú Orsi's official delegation to China, according to Montevideo Portal. Martín Gorrochategui, who operates a semiprecious stone quarry in Artigas department, was charged in February 2024 with exploiting 28 Venezuelan workers, prosecutor Sabrina Massaferro said. Gorrochategui traveled with the presidential mission that runs through February 7, representing MGG Art company alongside associate Zhu Wenda.

domestic_stories.title: Uruguay's Orsi says police warned him of tunnel robbery plot
domestic_stories.narrative: BEIJING, China — Uruguayan President Yamandú Orsi said police informed him more than a month ago about a possible tunnel robbery plot targeting banks in Montevideo's Old City, praising investigators' patience in the operation. Speaking from China during an official visit, Orsi said he received a call at 3 a.m. local time informing him that police had successfully thwarted the attempted heist. The plot involved 11 suspects from Uruguay, Brazil and Paraguay who dug a tunnel to sewers with plans to access bank branches, according to prosecutors who filed charges Wednesday.

domestic_stories.title: Opposition leader criticizes Orsi administration for dismantling predecessor's projects
domestic_stories.narrative: MONTEVIDEO, Uruguay — Opposition National Party leader Álvaro Delgado criticized President Yamandú Orsi's administration Saturday, saying it causes him "great sadness that a government dedicates itself to dismantling what the previous one did." Delgado said the current government has a "refoundational intention" to dismantle projects from former President Luis Lacalle Pou's administration, calling the approach "capricious" and "selfish." He cited the cancellation of the Neptune Project in Arazatí, a sanitation project for 190,000 Uruguayans in 61 interior localities, and the rescission of a contract with Cardama for two oceanic patrol boats.

domestic_stories.title: Uruguay's Orsi says 'things to resolve' before new port terminal
domestic_stories.narrative: SHANGHAI, China — Uruguayan President Yamandú Orsi said Thursday there are "many things to resolve before" considering installation of a new specialized terminal at Montevideo's port, following a court ruling that struck down restrictions on new terminals. Speaking during a state visit to China, Orsi said his administration will respect existing contracts while working to improve port operations through dialogue with operators. The Administrative Court partially upheld a challenge by port operator Montecon, striking down a clause that prevented new terminal permits until 2081.

Domestically, Orsi faced opposition criticism over his administration's approach to predecessor projects while indicating unresolved issues remain regarding a new port terminal development.

main_stories.title: Latvia PM Orders Investigation Into Epstein Case References
main_stories.narrative: RIGA, Latvia — Prime Minister Evika Siliņa ordered three government ministries to investigate references to Latvia found in newly released documents from convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein's case, according to her statement on social media platform X. The documents, released by the U.S. Justice Department in late January, mention Latvia more than 500 times and Riga more than 800 times as a potential recruitment location for underage girls, according to local media reports. Siliņa said the Interior Ministry, Welfare Ministry and Education and Science Ministry must work with other competent institutions to examine possible past events and assess current risks to children and youth. Latvia's State Police confirmed it has begun reviewing the materials and will cooperate with other Latvian institutions and request information through international cooperation channels.

main_stories.title: Latvia PM Supports Direct EU Talks with Russia on Ukraine
main_stories.narrative: DUBAI, United Arab Emirates — Latvian Prime Minister Evika Siliņa said the European Union should appoint a special envoy for direct negotiations with Russia regarding Ukraine, according to an interview with Euronews. Siliņa stated that while sanctions against Russia must continue, Europe needs diplomatic engagement and should "sit at the negotiating table" to help Ukraine in complex talks. Estonian President Alar Karis expressed similar views in the same interview, though Estonia's foreign ministry and prime minister later distanced themselves from Karis's statements, calling them unsuccessful.

main_stories.title: Latvia Opposition Breaks Quorum on Own No-Confidence Vote
main_stories.narrative: RIGA, Latvia — Opposition lawmakers in Latvia's parliament deliberately broke the voting quorum Thursday on their own motion to dismiss Prime Minister Evika Silina, preventing the sixth no-confidence vote against her from proceeding. The opposition coalition "Latvia First" had requested Silina's removal over migration policy, the Rail Baltica project oversight, and economic indicators, but 34 opposition deputies abstained from voting after heated debates. Only 47 of the required 50 lawmakers participated in the vote, with 46 rejecting the dismissal motion and one abstaining. Parliamentary Speaker Daiga Mierina suspended the session indefinitely, with the vote expected to resume next week.

main_stories.title: Latvian PM visits UAE to boost economic ties
main_stories.narrative: DUBAI, United Arab Emirates — Latvian Prime Minister Evika Siliņa concluded a working visit to the UAE aimed at strengthening economic cooperation and attracting investments, the Cabinet of Ministers said. Siliņa met with UAE President Sheikh Mohammed bin Zayed Al Nahyan and Vice President Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum to discuss cooperation in energy, logistics, data centers and healthcare sectors, according to government statements. The visit included signing a healthcare cooperation memorandum between the two countries' health ministers and meetings between Latvian companies and major investment fund Mubadala, which manages $380 billion in assets. Siliņa also participated in the World Governments Summit, described as one of the most significant global forums in the Gulf region.

international_stories.title: Latvia PM to attend Milan Winter Olympics opening ceremonies
international_stories.narrative: RIGA, Latvia — Prime Minister Evika Siliņa will travel to Italy Feb. 6-8 to attend the opening ceremonies of the XXV Winter Olympic Games in Milan and meet with Latvian Olympic athletes, the Cabinet of Ministers said. "The Olympic Games are a moment when the entire country is together with its athletes, and it is important to show respect for their contribution and express support on the path to the highest achievements," Siliņa said. During the visit, she will participate in an official reception hosted by Italian President Sergio Mattarella for heads of state and government, attend the opening ceremony, and join Latvia's official delegation evening in Milan. Latvia will be represented by a historically large delegation of 68 athletes competing in nine sports at the Milan-Cortina 2026 Winter Olympics.

The Prime Minister is actively pursuing international engagement through UAE economic visits and diplomatic positions on Russia-EU dialogue, potentially using foreign policy initiatives to bolster domestic standing amid political challenges.

Latvia's government is managing sensitive international issues simultaneously - investigating potential Epstein case connections while advocating for direct EU-Russia negotiations - requiring careful diplomatic balance to avoid controversy on multiple fronts.

main_stories.title: Canada drops EV sales quota amid auto industry pressure
main_stories.narrative: VAUGHAN, Ontario — Prime Minister Mark Carney announced Thursday that Canada will scrap its electric vehicle sales mandate, replacing the controversial policy with stricter tailpipe emissions standards and new purchase incentives. The government will eliminate the Electric Vehicle Availability Standard that required 100% zero-emission vehicle sales by 2035, responding to pressure from auto manufacturers and provincial leaders who called the timeline unrealistic. Carney said the new approach "focuses on the results that matter to Canadians, while avoiding placing undue burdens on the Canadian auto industry." The revised strategy aims for 75% EV adoption by 2035 and includes $2.3 billion in purchase incentives for vehicles under $50,000.

main_stories.title: Carney praises Harper at portrait unveiling ceremony
main_stories.narrative: OTTAWA, Canada — Prime Minister Mark Carney praised former Conservative leader Stephen Harper's fiscal record and crisis management during Tuesday's unveiling of Harper's official portrait on Parliament Hill. Harper, who served as prime minister from 2006 to 2015, called for unity between political parties against "external forces that threaten our independence" and internal separatist movements in Alberta and Quebec. The ceremony featured remarks from both leaders, with Carney noting Harper's pragmatic approach during the 2008 financial crisis and his advice over the past year. The portrait was painted by Canadian artist Phil Richards and attended by about 300 guests including former prime minister Jean Chrétien and Conservative Leader Pierre Poilievre.

main_stories.title: Carney announces Luxembourg visit, diplomatic appointments
main_stories.narrative: OTTAWA, Canada — Prime Minister Mark Carney announced that Luxembourg Prime Minister Luc Frieden will visit Canada from Feb. 7-9, 2026, to discuss strengthening partnerships in manufacturing, aerospace and financial services, his office said Tuesday. Carney also announced diplomatic appointments, naming former Defense Minister Bill Blair as High Commissioner to the United Kingdom and Nathalie G. Drouin as Ambassador to France and Monaco. The leaders will discuss NATO security issues and Russia's war against Ukraine during Frieden's visit, according to the Prime Minister's Office.

main_stories.title: Trump threatens tariffs over Carney's China trade deal
main_stories.narrative: WASHINGTON — President Donald Trump threatened 100 percent tariffs on Canada to prevent it from becoming China's "drop off port" for electric vehicles, following Prime Minister Mark Carney's recent trade agreement with Beijing. The deal allows limited Chinese EV imports to Canada in exchange for restored canola market access, according to trade experts and former diplomat Michael Kovrig. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent issued public warnings to Carney as mandatory USMCA trade pact reviews begin, with the U.S. positioned to use negotiations as leverage against both Canada and Mexico.
